learnCharts.title: How to read crochet charts
learnCharts.subtitle: Charts are a map of stitches. Learn a few symbols and you can follow diagrams without translating every abbreviation.
learnCharts.tip1: Each mark stands for a single action with your hook — not a whole row of fabric.
learnCharts.tip2: In rows, odd rows usually go right→left (or follow the arrows). In rounds, you work around the circle.
learnCharts.tip3: Open a technique page to see the symbol next to the how-to — then come back here for the full legend.
learnCharts.legendSubtitle: Same glyphs we use in Pattern Studio diagrams.
learnCharts.legendDc: T with a slash — double crochet (dc).
learnCharts.legendInc: V with crosses — increase (2 stitches in one).
learnCharts.legendMr: Circle with a center — magic ring (MR).
learnCharts.practiceSubtitle: Each page shows one symbol with the stitch you’re learning.

mr.title: Magic ring
mr.tip: A tight center for amigurumi — no hole in the middle.
frames: Make a loop with the yarn
Pull the tail to close the ring
steps: Wrap yarn around your fingers to form a ring, keeping a short tail.
Insert the hook into the ring, yarn over, and pull up a loop.
Work the stitches listed in the round into the ring.
Pull the yarn tail to close the center snug.

sc.title: Single crochet
sc.tip: The basic stitch for most amigurumi rounds.
frames: Yarn over and pull up a loop
Yarn over and pull through both loops
steps: Insert the hook under both top loops of the next stitch.
Yarn over and pull up a loop (2 loops on hook).
Yarn over again and pull through both loops — one sc made.

inc.title: Increase
inc.tip: Two stitches in the same place — the fabric grows.
frames: Work a second sc in the same stitch
Two stitches from one — that is an increase
steps: Find the stitch where the increase goes.
Work one single crochet into that stitch.
Work a second single crochet into the exact same stitch.
You now have two stitches from one — count them before the next round.

dec.title: Decrease
dec.tip: Two stitches become one — the fabric narrows.
frames: Pull up a loop from each stitch
Yarn over and pull through all loops
steps: Insert the hook into the next stitch and pull up a loop.
Insert into the following stitch and pull up another loop (3 loops on hook).
Yarn over and pull through all three loops — one stitch remains.

fo.title: Fasten off
fo.tip: Secure the last stitch so the work does not unravel.
frames: Yarn over and pull the tail through
Tighten — then weave in the end
steps: Cut the yarn, leaving a tail long enough to weave in (or sew pieces).
Yarn over and pull the tail all the way through the last loop.
Pull tight, then weave the end into the wrong side of the work.
